summary: Chinese has no articles. A bare noun is read as ‘the’ or ‘a’ from context and from its place in the sentence: a noun before the verb is usually known (西红柿在这里 ‘the tomatoes are here’), a noun after 有 is new (这里有西红柿 ‘there are tomatoes here’). 一 + measure word introduces one new thing (我买一个南瓜 ‘I buy a pumpkin’); 这/那 + measure word points at a known one (这个南瓜 ‘this pumpkin’).

rows: bare noun before the verb = known
一 + measure word = one new thing
这 + measure word when you must point

blocks.title: 这 is not ‘the’
blocks.text: 这个 means ‘this one’. Most English ‘the’ is simply nothing in Chinese.

traps: Do not translate ‘the’ word by word: 这 means ‘this’, not ‘the’.
Do not add 一个 for every English ‘a’: 这是西红柿 (‘this is a tomato’) and 我喜欢西红柿 (‘I like tomatoes’) need none.
A known thing goes before the verb: 西红柿在哪里？ ‘where is the tomato?’ — 哪里有西红柿？ asks ‘where can I find (any) tomatoes?’
